title: Medical Translator vs. Interpreter Differences and AI Safety
summary: Compare medical translators, interpreters, sight translation, AI safety risks, and current healthcare evidence. (October 2026)
body_markdown:
###


A medical translator works with written text. A medical interpreter works with spoken or signed communication. Translation can usually be reviewed before distribution, while interpretation requires quality controls during a live exchange.


###


Sight translation is the oral rendering of a written document in another language. It can help with short material during an encounter, but it does not provide a translated document for the patient to keep.


###


No single answer applies to every system or encounter. One 2026 Spanish simulation found mixed results across quality measures. Compare evidence by language, specialty, audio conditions, error type, and study design, then test the intended workflow.


###


Review the complete document for missing content, changed meaning, medication details, numbers, warnings, formatting, and readability. Match the review process to the document, its clinical importance, and current organizational and legal requirements.


###


Yes, but the workflows should remain distinct. Live interpretation needs turn-level monitoring and correction paths. Written translation needs complete-document checks, version control, and a distribution process appropriate to the material.
